correctness.rationale: A cyclic connected-prefix equivalence proves the complete state encoding; the exhaustive local swap classification yields degree and edge formulae. For root-fixed states a target-prefix insertion process achieves Kendall lower bound. For all-clockwise cyclic rotations, conservation of signed occupancy across every one of the n-1 cell interfaces yields a sharp (n-1) min(k,n-k) lower bound achieved by an explicit vacancy-transfer route. Direct permutation and independent bit-graph programs passed all asserted finite tests; those tests are corroboration, not the infinite proof.

broader_coverage.reasoning: The general theorem gives reconfiguration using width up to 2k, not paths in the optimum-width k layer. Its O(n^2) bound at doubled width cannot imply the exact optimum-layer distance or the precise k(k-1) detour. The separate pattern-avoiding result has a different feasible set.

value.rationale: General factor-two slack results do not resolve exact optimum-width movement. The result gives an infinite natural graph family with a complete move census, a large isometric rooted subclass, and a sharp quadratic detour for natural cyclic rotations, answering a feasible-layout shortest-path question with explicit optimal paths and dual conservation lower bounds.
